## Load data

```{r}
#| output: false
library("tidyverse")
library("broom")
library("ggrepel")
```

Load all the library needed.

```{r}
raw_dir <- "../data/_raw/"
data_file <- "gravier.RData"
data_loc <- "https://github.com/ramhiser/datamicroarray/raw/master/data/"

if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) {
  dir.create(path = raw_dir)
}

if (!file.exists(str_c(raw_dir, data_file))) {
  download.file(
    url = str_c(data_loc, data_file),
    destfile = str_c(raw_dir, data_file)
  )
}

load(file = str_c(raw_dir, data_file))
```

Importing the data using the code chunk given. Gravier is a dataset containing breast carcinoma data.

## Clean data

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug <- gravier |>
  bind_cols() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    y = case_when(
      y == "poor" ~ 1,
      y == "good" ~ 0
    )
  ) |>
  relocate(early_metastasis = y)
```

We process the raw `gravier` dataset by transforming the variable `y` into a binary numeric variable (1 for poor outcome, 0 for good outcome) and renaming it to `early_metastasis`.

## Analysis

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long <- gravier_clean_aug |> 
  pivot_longer(cols=starts_with("g"),
               names_to="gene",
               values_to="log2_expr_level")
```

To work on the dataset, we firstly convert it into a long format dataframe (tidy structure).

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long |> 
  group_by(gene) |> #group the rows for each gene 
  nest() |> #every group is nested into one different dataframe
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |> 
  group_by(gene) |>  
  mutate(model_object= map(.x = data, 
                   .f = ~lm(formula = log2_expr_level ~ early_metastasis,
                            data = .x)))   
```

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  mutate(model_object_tidy = map(.x = model_object,
                                 .f = ~ tidy(.x, conf.int =TRUE, conf.level = 0.95))
  )
```

We then nest the data by gene, so that each gene has its own tibble. After that, we fit a linear regression models to evaluate the association of each gene with early metastasis. Finally, we extract the models using `tidy()`, which organizes the data into a tidy tibble.

```{r}
gravier_estimates<- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |> 
  unnest(model_object_tidy)
```

```{r}
gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |> 
  filter(term=="early_metastasis") |> 
  select(-c(2:4,6,7)) |> 
  relocate(p.value, .before=estimate) |> 
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |> 
  mutate(q.value=p.adjust(p.value),
         is_significant=case_when(q.value>=0.05 ~ "no", q.value<0.05 ~ "yes"))
```

Before visualize the data we create another dataset (`gravier_estimates`), by keeping only the slope term. We then add a column containing the q-value (i.e. the p-value adjusted for multiple tests).
